chapter: Ellington, singers, the book and closing
title: Where the next improviser comes from; Scott LaFaro at the Showplace
summary: LaFaro slept in a chair at the Showplace; Mingus thinks he started bass playing for its own sake.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: About the future, there's something John Lewis said to me about 20 years ago, just been through a European tour and all that. He said, it could be -- and nobody knows when, that the next big improviser will come from Brazil or China or something else. Is that a possibility?
It might come from -- it won't come from Maynard Ferguson.
No.

But it might come from some little cat like Lafaro was. Scott Lafaro used to come to my job at the Showplace, put his feet up on a chair and go to sleep, every night. Matter of fact, the date I did with you, --
Yeah.
If my bass hadn't of broke, I'd of sounded a lot more like Scott Lafaro than Scott Lafaro
did. Because I'd been playing so long, my technique was much .
Yeah.
I was using the full range of the bass and I didn't just play how he played. Here's a -- little white guy like that might come as something new.
Somebody told me that he was probably to blame for a lot of what's going on in bass playing since then.
Scott LaFaro?
Yeah, playing up high, playing fast just to play fast.
He is to blame for it.
It's like technique is just there for its own sake.
Yeah, well, he'd sit there and say, how am I going to Charlie Mingus? He'd lay there and say that.
Yeah.
He never missed a stand. He just came very night, man, he'd hardly miss a night. I didn't know he was, so I said, who's th at cat over there sleeping in the chair?
Yeah.
That's Scott LaFaro. He's been there all week long. What's he doing here?
He never talked to you?
No.
That's peculiar.
He may have when I didn't know who he was.
